---
title: Fix a working copy that can't catch up
sidebar_label: Fix a working copy
description: Find the message a working copy shows when it can't catch up, belongs to another instance, was made by another build or has no room, and fix it.
job: A builder whose working copy can't catch up, or was made by another instance or build, finds the message and fixes it.
---

A working copy follows one instance through its event log: [Working copies](/build/working-copies) says what it holds and when it falls behind. No fix below loses a queued write. The CLI names the code and exits `4`, except where a section says otherwise.

## this working copy can no longer be kept current

```text
this working copy can no longer be kept current (reach_changed): what the credential may read, or how the server arranges items and types, has changed; rebuild the copy from the server (changes not yet sent are kept)
```

The code in brackets says why: `reach_changed`, `instance_changed`, `catchup_too_old`, `credential_ended`, `slice_changed` or `head_past_log`. Run `marfa device hydrate` again with the options the copy was filled with: it exits `2` without `--type` and `--tier`, and each `--edge-type` goes again. Leave out of `--type` any type the credential no longer reads. After `catchup_too_old` the copy is `stale` and answers reads until the hydrate fills it. After `credential_ended`, sign in or use a new key first.

## blocked, with the reason instance_changed

Another Marfa answers at the copy's address. The hydrate builds the copy from it and holds each waiting write `blocked`, so none reaches that instance unasked. Check `marfa device queue`, then `marfa device release --reason instance_changed`, or one ID, and `marfa device drain` to send. `marfa device withdraw <id>` drops one.

## this working copy is not waiting to be filled again in place

```text
this working copy is not waiting to be filled again in place (not_stale)
```

`marfa device hydrate --in-place-only` fills only a copy whose cursor the event log let go. This one is whole, or was never built. Run `marfa device catch-up` to bring it up to date, or `marfa device hydrate` with the same `--type`, `--tier` and `--edge-type` options, and without `--in-place-only`, to build it again.

## this file belongs to

```text
this file belongs to https://marfa.example, not https://other.example
```

The code is `wrong_server`. The device was offered another origin than the copy recorded, so it refused before it sent a credential or a write, and named both. **Nothing was sent.** Point the device back at the copy's origin, or open a new working copy for the other. A different instance at the recorded origin gives `copy_expired` with `instance_changed` instead. In Swift, `wrongServer` carries `expected` and `got`.

## was made by another build of the core

```text
copy.sqlite was made by another build of the core (last saved by release 0.0.86): …
```

A build with another schema won't open the file, and **nothing is deleted.** With no unsent writes, hydrate at a new `--db` path. Otherwise [install the release](/reference/cli#install) the message names, run `marfa device drain`, and **keep the old file while `marfa device unsent` lists a write**: `discard` takes only refused ones, with their edit. Then install the current release and hydrate at a new `--db` path. Swift's `ifRefused: .replace` replaces the store only if no write is unsent.

## local storage is full

The code is `storage_full`. The volume is full, so the copy didn't open, even to read. The CLI exits `3` and Swift throws `storageFull`. Free room and open it again.

## not replaced

```text
not replaced: app.reading (the server's code): the server's message
```

The hydration reports it in `unreplaced_types` (`unreplacedTypes` in Swift). An app declared an `app.*` type that the instance holds in another definition, and a key without `schema.write` can't replace it. The hydration finished, and **the type stays as the instance holds it**, so a write that relies on the new definition may be refused. Hydrate again with a credential that may change the type, or change the declaration to match.
